record.context_brief: Least-energy sign-changing solution in 4D spectral case
record.original_question: For the four-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, possibly convex or even strictly star-shaped, does there exist a least-energy sign-changing solution when lambda belongs to the Dirichlet spectrum sigma(-Delta)? Here least-energy means a sign-changing critical point that minimizes the associated energy among the sign-changing states on the sign-changing Nehari manifold described in the paper.

evidence.quote: u-hat is called the least-energy sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1).

Open question 11: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could be convex or even strictly star-sharped, does there exist least-energy sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) for N = 4 and lambda in sigma(-Delta)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary (which may be assumed convex, or even strictly star-shaped, if necessary). Consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem in dimension $N=4$:
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2}u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
where $2^* = \tfrac{2N}{N-2} = 4$ is the critical Sobolev exponent. Let $\sigma(-\Delta)$ denote the Dirichlet spectrum of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, i.e., the sequence of eigenvalues $0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\le\lambda_3\le\cdots$ of $-\Delta$ with zero boundary conditions on $\Omega$.

The associated energy functional on $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is
$$I_\lambda(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx - \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\int_\Omega u^2\,dx - \tfrac{1}{4}\int_\Omega u^4\,dx.$$
Define the sign-changing Nehari manifold
$$\mathcal{M}_\lambda = \bigl\{u\in H^1_0(\Omega):\, u^\pm\not\equiv 0,\; \langle I'_\lambda(u),u^+\rangle = \langle I'_\lambda(u),u^-\rangle = 0\bigr\},$$
where $u^+=\max\{u,0\}$ and $u^-=\min\{u,0\}$. A function $\hat u\in\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ is called a least-energy sign-changing solution if $\hat u$ is a critical point of $I_\lambda$ with $\hat u^\pm\not\equiv 0$ and
$$I_\lambda(\hat u) = \inf\{I_\lambda(u):\, u\in\mathcal{M}_\lambda\}.$$

Question: For every $\lambda\in\sigma(-\Delta)$, does there exist a least-energy sign-changing solution of the above problem?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on the 4D Brezis–Nirenberg problem establishes existence of nontrivial solutions for λ outside the Dirichlet spectrum, and constructs sign-changing/blowing-up solutions in various regimes, but the existence of a least-energy sign-changing solution in a general bounded (possibly convex or strictly star-shaped) domain when λ ∈ σ(−Δ) is listed among the open questions in surveys on the problem. No resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: The Brezis-Nirenberg problem in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: For N=4 and λ>0, provided λ is not in the spectrum σ(−Δ), the Brezis–Nirenberg problem admits a nontrivial solution.
status_evidence.claim: Existing 4D results require λ ∉ σ(−Δ); the spectral case remains delicate.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis-Nirenberg problems: Open questions and new results in dimension six
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on the Brezis–Nirenberg problem alongside new dimension-six results.
status_evidence.claim: Open questions about least-energy sign-changing solutions in the 4D spectral case are recorded in recent surveys.
